about: AI agent harness features derived bottom-up from the use cases in design/ai/agent-use-cases.md, and the map from every use case to the features it needs. Companion to agent-harness-features.md.

needs.essential: the use case cannot be done without the feature
needs.helpful: the feature makes the result better, safer or easier but is not required

step: The step of the use case that calls for the feature, when one was recorded; empty when the tag came from a consistency rule.

families.name: Conversation and context
families.summary: Holding a task, its history and its referents together across turns, sessions and very large material.

families.name: Asking the user
families.summary: Getting the information a task needs from the person, in the right form and order.

families.name: Planning and orchestration
families.summary: Turning goals into steps, splitting work among helpers, recovering from failure and reusing what worked.

families.name: Memory and knowledge
families.summary: What the agent remembers about people and projects, and the reference knowledge it consults instead of guessing.

families.name: Graph and product tools
families.summary: The agent's hands inside the product: reading, building, analyzing, styling and showing graphs, and operating the interface.

families.name: Information gathering
families.summary: Finding and reading material from the outside world, politely and within its terms.

families.name: Files, documents and media
families.summary: Reading what people supply in any form and producing files, documents, figures and media for them.

families.name: Execution and compute
families.summary: Where and how computation runs: sandboxes, scaled jobs, model pipelines, headless copies, devices and solvers.

families.name: Integrations and outbound actions
families.summary: Connecting to outside systems, accounts, agents and devices, and acting in them.

families.name: Long-running and proactive work
families.summary: Work that continues without the user present, starts on its own, and reaches the user later.

families.name: Human control and trust
families.summary: Keeping the person in charge: previews, approvals, limits, interruption and hand-offs.

families.name: Quality and verification
families.summary: Checking results, saying how sure the agent is, and testing the agent itself.

families.name: Provenance, reproducibility and audit
families.summary: Where every value came from, how every result was made, and what every action was.

families.name: Observability
families.summary: Seeing what the agent and the product are doing while it happens.

families.name: Explanation and communication
families.summary: Saying things clearly, to the right audience, in the right language, fast enough.

families.name: Interaction modes and channels
families.summary: Every way in and out besides typing in the main window: voice, pointing, devices, phones, small screens and non-visual output.

families.name: Safety
families.summary: Recognizing harm, slowing risky requests, framing advice and protecting people physically and emotionally.

families.name: Privacy and data governance
families.summary: Controlling what personal data is collected, kept, shown, sent and inferred.

families.name: Security
families.summary: Keeping hostile content, hostile files and secrets from subverting the agent.

families.name: Identity, access and collaboration
families.summary: Who is acting, what they may see and do, and how several people work together.

families.name: Cost and performance
families.summary: Knowing what work will cost and keeping it within limits.

features.name: Multi-turn task conversation
features.definition: Hold one task open across many back-and-forth turns, keeping the goal, earlier answers, choices and intermediate results in play.
features.includes: Follow-ups that build on earlier results; corrections that revise an earlier step; switching between related sub-questions without losing the main task.
features.why: Tasks whose first step is an interview or an 'ask which accounts, which city, which kind of graph' exchange, tasks refined over several rounds (cleaning loops, styling, drafting), and games and coaching where each turn depends on the last. Without it every follow-up starts from nothing.

features.name: Long-session context and transcript recall
features.definition: Keep a long session coherent when its history outgrows what the agent can hold at once, and search, quote and recall the agent's own past turns as data.
features.includes: Summarizing older turns; pinning decisions and constraints so they survive summarization; searching and quoting earlier turns; recalling an earlier decision on demand.
features.why: Sessions that run for hours or days (an iterative cleaning loop, a document pile worked through, a caption-first collaboration) where the agent must quote what it said earlier or recall a decision made long ago, and must not lose pinned constraints when older turns are condensed.

features.name: Large-material handling
features.definition: Work over graphs, files and corpora far larger than the agent's context by computing, sampling, profiling and retrieving instead of reading everything.
features.includes: Chunking and indexing; compact graph profiles (counts, distributions, schema, samples); streaming parse; reading the head or a sample of a huge file; retrieving pieces on demand.
features.why: Steps that read a corpus, log set, transaction export, single-cell matrix or repository far larger than the agent can read at once, and steps that 'summarize big graphs first'. The agent must profile, sample, chunk and retrieve rather than read.

features.name: Reference resolution
features.definition: Resolve words like 'this', 'these two', 'my cousin' or 'that step' to concrete graph elements, UI controls, earlier results or people.
features.includes: Using the current selection, pointer target, recent results and conversation history as referents; asking when a reference is ambiguous.
features.why: Steps where the user says 'this', 'these two clusters', 'my cousin' or 'the step where the colors changed' and the agent must bind the words to a node, a region, a saved project or an earlier result, often from pointing, gaze or selection, and ask when several match.

features.name: User activity awareness
features.definition: Observe what the user is doing and has done in the product (clicks, selections, camera moves, undos, errors, features used) as context for help.
features.includes: A live stream of user and app events; opted-in history of sessions, projects and features used; error signals. Frame-rate figures belong to F124.
features.why: Help, teaching and accessibility steps that watch what the user does: noticing repeated undos or an abandoned control, a freshly loaded file, which features a user never touches, or a tangent the user has started, so that help arrives at the right moment.

features.name: Time and date awareness
features.definition: Every feature must know the current date and time and reason correctly about time zones, calendars, recurrence, deadlines and time windows. A quality attribute, not a separately built feature.
features.includes: Relative dates ('last spring'); recurrence rules; timeline windows over data; staleness of facts.
features.why: Steps that reason over dated data (tie strength per year, monthly reply graphs, timelines over decades), schedule or remind (before each birthday, maintenance reminders), check freshness, or interpret 'last spring'. It is a quality every other feature must have.

features.name: Hidden state keeping
features.definition: Hold information the user must not see yet (a puzzle answer, a game secret) and reveal it only by a stated rule.
features.includes: Secrets kept out of displayed output and tool results shown to the user; rule-driven reveals.
features.why: Games, puzzles, lessons and evaluations where the agent computes an answer, a culprit, a spoiler or an exam key and must keep it out of everything the user sees until a rule says to reveal it.

features.name: User state inference
features.definition: With opt-in, estimate whether the user is right now stuck, overloaded, nauseous, distressed or tired, with a confidence and a limit on false alarms, and adjust pace, detail and interruptions.
features.includes: Signals from activity, speech and body; confidence; false-alarm limits; adaptation of pace and detail.
features.why: Steps that estimate, with opt-in, whether the user is overloaded, stuck or nauseous and adjust pace and detail.

features.name: Clarifying questions
features.definition: Decide when a request is ambiguous or underspecified and what to ask before committing to an interpretation (when and what to ask; the form of the question is F10).
features.includes: Detecting ambiguity in intent or data meaning; deciding when to ask versus assume; a free-text escape on every choice question.
features.why: First steps of most tasks: 'ask the occasion, audience and length', 'ask which trackers they use', 'ask which show and the last episode watched'. The agent must judge which unknowns block progress and which it may assume.

features.name: Structured questions
features.definition: Ask the user a question with typed choices, checkboxes, ranges, pickers or a small form and get a machine-readable answer.
features.includes: Option lists, sliders, thresholds, date ranges, field forms; validation of the answer; defaults the user can accept.
features.why: Steps that need a precise, machine-readable answer: a merge policy per kind, a unit and currency, an edge threshold, which attributes to map to sound, a role from a short list, never-send marks per column. A form or picker avoids misreading free text.

features.name: Interpretation echo-back
features.definition: Restate in plain words what the agent understood (the request, a translated query, the selected set, what it heard) so the user can correct it. What an action will change is F100.
features.includes: Natural-language to graph-query translation shown back for editing; spoken-command confirmation; showing the selected set.
features.why: Steps that translate the user's words into something executable (a query, a set of filters, a lasso selection, a spoken destructive command, a drawn sketch) and must show that reading back before acting on it.

features.name: Scripted step-by-step sessions
features.definition: Run an ordered, resumable, multi-step dialog in one of two paces: agent-paced (an interview that fills a structured record from the answers) or user-paced (coaching the user through steps they do themselves, waiting for each and never doing it for them unasked).
features.includes: Question and step sequencing; skip and return; resume across sessions; building graph data from answers; steps in outside systems; confirming each step before cueing the next.
features.why: Long guided interviews that fill a graph (name generators, care-team maps, gift ledgers, survey calls) and coaching sessions that walk a user through steps they do themselves (requesting a data export, a first tour), both needing order, skip and resume.

features.name: Game and lesson session engine
features.definition: Own the rules of games and lessons: turns, scoring, timers, hidden answers and reveal rules (F08), learner mastery, and deciding what a learner reviews next and when.
features.includes: Turns, scores, timers; reveal rules; mastery tracking; spaced repetition and flashcard ordering.
features.why: Games and lessons with turns, scores, timers, hidden answers, mastery tracking and spaced review.

features.name: Planning
features.definition: Break a goal into an ordered plan of steps with dependencies before acting, and revise it as results arrive or steps fail. Showing the plan for edits is F15.
features.includes: Dependency ordering; re-planning on new facts or failures.
features.why: Steps that turn a goal into an ordered pipeline (fetch, resolve, build, analyze, report), split work among helpers, plan a lesson or tour, or plan a staged sequence where order matters for safety, then revise as results arrive.

features.name: Shared plan and task list
features.definition: Keep one visible, editable plan or list of steps and parked items with their state (pending, done, blocked) that both the user and the agent see, edit and reorder, and that survives interruptions.

features.why: Steps that show the plan as a checklist, pin the main goal as a visible card, turn a quality report into a task queue, or track which checks came back, so the user and agent see and edit the same list across interruptions.

features.name: Sub-agents
features.definition: Spawn helper agents with isolated context. Mechanism: parallel fan-out over sources, entities, batches or sub-questions, result merging, and per-agent limits. Configuration: each agent's role, stance or persona, its restricted knowledge and tools, and which model or method it uses (via F167).
features.includes: Fan-out and merge; lead, worker, reviewer and specialist roles; persona agents with deliberately restricted knowledge; hand-off rules between agents. Debate, judging and critique protocols are F110; interacting populations are F181.
features.why: Steps that fan out one helper per portal, source, hypothesis, persona or batch; reviewer, critic and researcher roles; persona agents that must know only what their persona knows; exams run in clean sessions.

features.name: Error recovery and self-repair
features.definition: Detect failures (timeouts, bad parses, tool errors, missing data, schema changes), diagnose the cause, retry or change approach within limits, and explain what happened in plain words.
features.includes: Retry with backoff; repairing inputs; switching methods; clear failure reports when it gives up.
features.why: Steps that hit timeouts, parse errors, missing dates or failed downloads and must split the query, read the error and the offending region, retry another way, or set a file aside with the reason.

features.name: Reusable recipes
features.definition: Capture a working procedure built from existing tools (query, crawl, pipeline, analysis) as a named, parameterized recipe that can be inspected, edited and rerun on new inputs. New code against extension points is F50.
features.includes: Condensing a session's operation log into a recipe; rerun to refresh.
features.why: Steps that capture a working import, query, crawl or analysis as a named procedure and rerun it on new data or on a schedule ('rerun the query to refresh', 'record the session as a replayable recipe').

features.name: Cross-session user memory
features.definition: Remember a user's or team's preferences, past sources, decisions and lessons, including a learned writing voice, and apply them in later sessions.

features.why: Steps that recall a user's language, sensitivities, liked and rejected sources, usual look, mastery or long-running projects in a later session ('remember the topic and seeds for future updates', 'recall the student's misconceptions').

features.definition: Show the user what the agent remembers about them and let them inspect, correct and remove individual memories. Finding and deleting content everywhere with proof is F151.

features.name: Memory isolation
features.definition: Keep memory and data partitioned per project or client, with explicit, permissioned linking across partitions.
features.includes: Per-project memory scopes; deliberate cross-project links; no leakage between clients.
features.why: Investigation and client work where each matter's or client's terms, entities and decisions must stay in their own partition and never leak into another.

features.name: Domain knowledge packs
features.definition: Install, version and trust packs of domain knowledge: procedures, checklists, glossaries, reference facts, method assumptions and caveats, standards, and rules by jurisdiction, consulted instead of relying on model recall alone.
features.includes: Procedures and checklists; maintained terminology glossaries; method assumptions and interpretation rules; laws and rules by jurisdiction with when a qualified person must review; pack versioning and trust.
features.why: Steps that depend on reference knowledge the model should not guess: null models and multiple-comparison corrections, kinship terms, country codes and disputed territories, which privacy rules apply in a jurisdiction, field vocabulary.

features.name: Semantic retrieval
features.definition: Index text and items by meaning and search them, finding nearest neighbors and near-duplicates across a corpus or the project.
features.includes: Embedding indexes; similarity search; duplicate detection among issues, requests or records.
features.why: Steps that find items by meaning rather than by exact words: nearest papers to an abstract, duplicate issues or feature requests, requirements matched to controls, themes across many messages, missing links by text similarity.
